The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though appeal is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.
2. Challenging order of award dated 10.08.2020 passed by II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner for Employee's Compensation, Vijayapur ('Commisioner' for short) in ECA no.46/2015, this appeal is filed.
3. Shri Sanganagouda V.Biradar, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that since insurer was not in appeal,
finding of Commissioner regarding relationship of employer and employee and occurrence of incident in course and out of employment NC: 2023:KHC-K:7402 and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.

4. Only ground on which enhancement is sought is that monthly income of deceased taken was contrary to Section 4(1B) of Employee's Compensation Act ('E.C. Act' for short) and failure to award funeral expenses contrary to Section 4(4) of E.C.Act.
5.
It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 15.12.2015, deceased Shekhar was aged 28 years working as driver and earning `10,000/- per month apart from `100/- per day as bhatta.

However,
contrary to Section 4(1B) of E.C.Act, Commissioner considered it at `4,000/- per month and awarded meager compensation.
Even failure to award funeral expenses was contrary to provision of Section 4(4) of E.C.Act.

sentences.text: On other hand, Shri Subhash Mallapur learned counsel for respondent no.2/insurer supported order.
Heard learned counsel for parties.
Perused impugned order and records.

8. From above submission, following substantial questions of law are taken-up for examination :
"(i) Whether assessment of monthly income by Commissioner is contrary to Section 4(1B) of E.C.Act ?
(ii) Whether Commissioner erred in not awarding compensation towards funeral expenses?"
9.
Admittedly, accident occurred on 15.12.2014 i.e., after coming into force of amending Act no.45 of 2009 of E.C.Act inserting Section 4(1B) in EC Act.
By virtue of said insertion, Central Government was authorized to notify income for purposes of Section 4.
In terms of said authorization, Central Government issued notification no.S.O.1258(E) with effect from 31.05.2010 notifying `8,000/- as income for purposes of sub-section (1) of E.C.Act.

As in impugned order, Commissioner determined monthly income at `4,000/-, contrary to law, substantial NC: 2023:KHC-K:7402 question of law no.(i) would arise for consideration and is answered by holding that monthly income of deceased has to be considered at `8,000/-.
In view of above finding, compensation awardable would be `8,47,160/- (8,000 X 50% X 211.79).
10. Further, in view of Section 4(4) of E.C.Act, award of not less than `5,000/- towards funeral expenses would be mandatory.
Normally, in case of death under Motor Vehicles Act, sum of `15,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses.
Failure to award same, would be contrary to Section 4(4) of E.C.Act.
Therefore, claimants are held entitled for `15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Substantial question of law no.(ii) arises for consideration is answered in favour of appellants.

Thus,
following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Claimants are held entitled for total compensation of `8,72,160/- with interest at 12% per annum from 15.01.2015 till deposit from insurer.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7402 (iii) Insurer shall deposit said compensation within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
